source.extraction: First HTML pre block; remove HTML tags, HTML-unescape once, UTF-8 encode; preserve leading and trailing whitespace.

differences: C updates planet pointers and YIAN updates entries through a checked Planet[] slice; both traverse i then j=i+1, apply pairwise velocity updates, and then update all positions in body order.
Both accumulate kinetic energy followed by each i<j potential term in the same body and expression order using f64 values.
Both accumulate momentum in body order and update the Sun velocity using solar_mass.
C reads steps from argv and has file-scope bodies; YIAN uses its bench-scale step marker and initializes the five bodies in a local fixed array.

Both apply offset_momentum once, print initial energy, advance by 0.01 exactly n times, and print final energy. YIAN prints both energies through the standard library's nine-digit fixed specification, which reproduces the C printf precision.
